name: Dongotono
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Muratori, Carlo. 1938. Grammatica Lotuxo. Verona: Missioni Africane (archive.org full view); pp. xvii, 471-473 on 'Donotono'
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number KF 21547) (also digitized at HathiTrust, search-only (in copyright))
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number KF 21547
sources.note: accent remarks (sec. 49, p. 18) concern Lotuxo proper; Dongotono appears only in classification and word comparisons (e.g. p. 472 'terra.. Donotono kwaf').

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: all hits classificatory, ethnographic, encyclopaedic or bibliographic (Tucker & Bryan 1956 handbook, Heine et al. Die Sprachen Afrikas, Seligman 1932, Ethnologue editions, etc.); no descriptive text on Dongotono sound structure beyond the Vossen Rosetta excerpt.

sources.citation: Moodie, Jonathan. 2019. A grammar of the Lopit language. (Lopit grammar; sec. 1 on Lotuxo languages, Vossen wordlist sample incl. Dongotono)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: nothing on Dongotono phonology; cites only Vossen 1982 and Driberg 1932 for Dongotono.

sources.citation: Muniru, John. 2019. Sociolinguistic assessment of Lango, Imotong, Logir, Okolie (Lorwama and Ketebo) and Dongotono speech varieties of Torit State, South Sudan: a summary of findings. Juba: SIL South Sudan. 8 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: nothing; lexicostatistics/RTT/vitality only; gives autonym [dōŋōtónò] with tone marks.

sources.citation: Billington, Rosey. 2017. The phonetics and phonology of the Lopit language. PhD thesis, University of Melbourne (ch. 2 review of Nilotic phonology, pp. 44, 64, 69-70, 73-74)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: second-hand only: p. 69 'For Dongotono, Lokoya and Lopit, Vossen (1982) records High, Low, Mid and High-Falling tones, as for Otuho'; p. 64 Vossen finds no distinctive vowel length in Dongotono; pp. 73-74 general remark that for Eastern Nilotic 'there is little mention of [stress] in later descriptive work' apart from no-contrastive-stress statements for Turkana and Otuho. No stress statement for Dongotono.

sources.citation: Vossen 1982 (same book) -- Rosetta 'phon' excerpts for Karimojong (7.2.2.1, pp. 178-181), Turkana, Bari (7.2.1.1, pp. 171-175), read to establish the template of Vossen's per-language phonology notes
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: no stress subsection anywhere: each language gets Consonants / Vowels / Tone; p. 175 'As tone is not of much importance in my comparative study of Eastern Nilotic, no emphasis is laid on the analysis of its functions'. Nothing on Dongotono in these pages.

sources.citation: Vossen, Rainer. 1982. The Eastern Nilotes: Linguistic and Historical Reconstructions (Kölner Beiträge zur Afrikanistik 9). Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. -- Rosetta Project excerpt for [ddd], pp. 165-166, sec. 7.1.11 Dongotono
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: nothing; excerpt is speaker numbers and informant notes only. The book's Dongotono phonology (sec. 7.2 'LOTUKO dialects', pp. 189-193) is not in any Rosetta excerpt.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Dongotono language' and (fr) 'Dongotono', wikitext via API, used as page locators into Vossen 1982
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: nothing on stress; en article (citing Vossen 1982:189-193) reports consonant/vowel inventories and 'four tones in Dongotono: High, Low, Mid, and High-Falling.. used for both lexical and grammatical contrasts' (p. 193).

sources.citation: Schadeberg, Thilo C. & M. Lionel Bender (eds.) 1981. Nilo-Saharan: Proceedings of the First Nilo-Saharan Linguistics Colloquium, Leiden 1980. Dordrecht: Foris. Incl. Vossen, R., 'The classification of Eastern Nilotic and its significance for ethnohistory', pp. 41ff

sources.note: nothing on Dongotono prosody; Dongotono appears only in the Lotuko-group tree (p. 45) and in Muratori's subgrouping quoted p. 43.
